2. Prohibited practices

Stage 2 · question 1 · PDF 2.1 · p. 5

1. Does the tool, or its intended use, involve: (AI Act, art. 5 § 1) • (1) [point a] using subliminal, manipulative or deceptive techniques to materially alter a person's behaviour, risking significant harm to that person? • (2) [point b] exploiting a person's vulnerability due to age, disability or social or economic situation to materially alter their behaviour, risking significant harm to that person? • (3) [point ba] (from 2 December 2026) generating or modifying realistic images, videos, audio or similar content showing an identifiable person's intimate parts, or that person engaged in sexually explicit activity, without their freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous and explicit consent? • (4) [point bb] (from 2 December 2026) generating or modifying child sexual abuse material or a pornographic performance involving a child within the meaning of article 2, points c and e, of Directive 2011/93/EU? • (5) [point c] scoring or classifying people according to their social behaviour or personal characteristics (social scoring), resulting in unjustified or disproportionate unfavourable treatment? • (6) [point d] assessing the risk that a person will commit an offence solely on the basis of profiling or personality traits? • (7) [point e] creating or expanding a facial recognition database through untargeted collection of images (internet, CCTV)? • (8) [point f] inferring people's emotions in their workplace or an educational institution, except for medical or safety reasons? • (9) [point g] categorising people using biometric data to infer their race, political opinions, trade union membership, religious or philosophical beliefs, sex life or sexual orientation? • (10) [point h] identifying people biometrically, remotely and in real time in a publicly accessible space for law enforcement purposes? Answers:

Answered — No, none

Check satisfied on the declared answer

Stage 2 · question 2 · PDF 2.2 · p. 5

AI ACT 2. Will the tool be used for any of the following purposes? (AI Act, art. 6 and annexes I and III) • (1) Education: admissions, assessment of learning outcomes, assigning an educational level, examination monitoring [annex III, point 3] • (2) Employment: recruitment, selection, promotion, assessment, task allocation, dismissal [annex III, point 4] • (3) Biometrics: remote identification, biometric categorisation, emotion recognition [annex III, point 1] • (4) Access to public assistance, such as grants (classification to verify) [annex III, point 5(a)] • (5) A safety component of a regulated product, such as a medical device [annex I] Answers:

Answered — No

Check satisfied on the declared answer

Stage 2 · question 3 · PDF 2.3 · p. 6

AI ACT 3. Will UNIL be considered the tool's “provider”? This applies if: (AI Act, art. 3 § 3 and art. 25 § 1) • (1) UNIL develops, or has developed, an AI system that it puts into service under its own name; • (2) UNIL puts its name or trademark on a high-risk system already on the market; • (3) UNIL substantially modifies a high-risk system; • (4) UNIL changes a system's intended purpose (including general-purpose AI) so that it becomes high-risk. Answers:

Answered — None of these cases: UNIL uses the tool as supplied and is the “deployer”
